item.title: She isn't just sewing a dress. She's growing one
item.description: In an age of fast fashion, author Eve Schaub wanted to go back to basics by growing a dress in her backyard. She's been working on her linen dress for over a year and still has a ways to go.

item.title: Comedian Jeff Arcuri talks about the art of crowd work
item.description: NPR's A Martinez talks with comedian Jeff Arcuri about the stand-up comic art of crowd work, which involves talking to audience members and ad-libbing off what they say.

item.title: What a forbidden hug from a nurse during lockdown meant to one a cancer patient
item.description: Shortly after the COVID-19 lockdown began, Ashleigh Bell Pedersen was diagnosed with an aggressive form of breast cancer. She came to desperately miss physical touch during treatment.

item.title: Kennedy Center must pay $250,000 in legal fees to musician who canceled in protest
item.description: Chuck Redd canceled his annual Christmas Eve performance to protest Trump's name being added to the complex. In June, a superior court judge dismissed the Kennedy Center's lawsuit against Redd.

item.title: 'Spider-Man' director found his connection to the world at the movies
item.description: Destin Daniel Cretton grew up in Maui, and says movies expanded his perspective: "I have always found movies to be a way of peering into other lives that I would never otherwise experience," he explains.

item.title: 'The Nerd Reich' tracks the 'unmasking of Silicon Valley's true politics'
item.description: Journalist Gil Durán argues that a small circle of Silicon Valley billionaires and venture capitalists have concluded that democracy is in their way — and that they should be governing in its place.

item.title: Aretha Franklin's 'Sparkle' soundtrack is a neglected classic
item.description: The 1976 film is about a '60s trio based loosely on The Supremes. It wasn't a big hit, but it has a devoted cult following, and critic Ken Tucker says it features some of Aretha Franklin's finest performances.
